- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; apply a “lag correction” — delay downward trend by 2–3 days or reduce slope of decline.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops sharply, model underestimates further decline; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); model often fails to revert to 30-day moving average; align forecast to 30-day MA if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often misreads “sell-off” as “recovery”; if sentiment >0.67 and price drops >2%, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is below 65 and sentiment is positive, model is likely underestimating rebound; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- In high-sentiment + high-price context, model often fails to capture “event-driven” price spikes; if sentiment >0.75 and price >75, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3 days.
